overview.historicalContext: Cap sets — subsets of $\{0,1,2\}^n$ with no three collinear points (i.e., no $x,y,z$ with $x+z=2y$ in $\mathbb{F}_3^n$) — arose from the study of arithmetic progressions in finite geometry. Leo Moser posed the problem and constructed cap sets of size $\Omega(3^n/\sqrt{n})$ using coordinate-sum restrictions. Hillel Furstenberg and Yitzhak Katznelson (1991) proved the density Hales-Jewett theorem using ergodic theory, implying $f_3(n) = o(3^n)$. Roy Meshulam (1995) gave the first quantitative bound $f_3(n) \leq 3^n/n$ using Fourier-analytic methods. The breakthrough came in 2016 when Jordan Ellenberg and Dion Gijswijt, building on Croot-Lev-Pach's polynomial method, proved $f_3(n) \leq c^n$ with $c = 3 \cdot (207 + 33\sqrt{33})^{1/3}/8 \approx 2.756$. This resolved a central problem in additive combinatorics and had immediate implications for the sunflower conjecture and other problems.
overview.problemStatement:
**Question:** Is f₃(n) = o(3^n)?

**Answer: YES** (Furstenberg-Katznelson 1991)

Let f₃(n) = max size of a subset of {0,1,2}^n with no three collinear points.

The density Hales-Jewett theorem implies cap sets have density → 0.
overview.text: Is f₃(n) = o(3^n) where f₃(n) is the max cap set in {0,1,2}^n? YES - Proved via density Hales-Jewett (Furstenberg-Katznelson 1991).
overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization defines:

1. **TernaryHypercube:** {0,1,2}^n as Fin n → ZMod 3
2. **OnLine:** Collinearity via x + z = 2y
3. **CombinatorialLine:** Lines in Hales-Jewett sense
4. **IsCapSet:** No three collinear points
5. **f3(n):** Maximum cap set size

We axiomatize the density Hales-Jewett theorem and derive f₃(n) = o(3^n).
keyInsights: **Lines generalize APs:** In {0,1,2}^n, lines correspond to arithmetic progressions in certain embeddings.
**Density Hales-Jewett:** Any dense subset contains a combinatorial line, so cap sets have vanishing density.
**Moser's construction:** Points with coordinate sum ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 3) form large cap sets.
**Ellenberg-Gijswijt breakthrough:** Used polynomial method to show f₃(n) ≤ c^n with c < 3.
**OEIS A003142:** Records known values of f₃(n).

sections.title: Overview — Imports and Setup
sections.summary: Imports (Asymptotics, special functions, liminf/limsup topology), open Asymptotics Filter, and namespace Erdos185. Sets up the formalization of Erdős problem #185 on cap-set growth: the maximum size f₃(n) of a subset of {0,1,2}ⁿ containing no combinatorial line.
sections.mathContext: Module setup: imports, open Asymptotics Filter, namespace Erdos185

sections.title: Part I: Basic Definitions
sections.summary: TernaryHypercube n := Fin n → ZMod 3 and hypercube_card establishing |{0,1,2}ⁿ| = 3ⁿ. The ambient space in which cap sets live.

sections.title: Part II: Lines in {0,1,2}^n
sections.summary: OnLine and CombinatorialLine definitions: a combinatorial line is a maximal family of points agreeing on fixed coordinates and ranging together over {0,1,2} on the moving coordinates. These are the configurations cap sets must avoid.

sections.title: Part III: Cap Sets
sections.summary: IsCapSet and IsCapSetCombinatorial define line-free subsets; f3(n) is the maximum cap-set cardinality. Equivalence of the geometric (no 3-term AP / line) and combinatorial formulations.

sections.title: Part IV: Connection to Arithmetic Progressions
sections.summary: R3(N), the cap-set / 3-AP connection: f3 ≥ R3 lower bound relating cap sets in {0,1,2}ⁿ to progression-free sets, situating the problem within additive combinatorics.

sections.title: Part V: Known Bounds
sections.summary: Moser's lower bound and explicit construction, recording the classical lower bounds on f₃(n) prior to the density Hales–Jewett and polynomial-method results.

sections.title: Part VI: The Main Result — Density Hales–Jewett
sections.summary: The density Hales–Jewett theorem and its corollary f₃(n) = o(3ⁿ): cap sets have density tending to zero, the central qualitative answer to Erdős #185.
sections.mathContext: Density Hales–Jewett theorem; corollary f₃(n) = o(3ⁿ)

sections.title: Part VII: More Recent Progress
sections.summary: Meshulam (1995) and Ellenberg–Gijswijt (2016) polynomial-method bounds, with capSetConstant ≈ 2.756 recording the exponential base of the Ellenberg–Gijswijt upper bound f₃(n) ≤ O(2.756ⁿ).

sections.title: Part VIII: Examples
sections.summary: Small-case values of f₃, beginning with f3_1 : f3 1 = 2. Establishes the base of the explicit-computation tower continued in Parts VIII-A through VIII-F.

sections.title: Part VIII-A: f₃(2) = 4 — Explicit Computation
sections.summary: f3_2 : f3 2 = 4, proved by explicit enumeration of cap sets in {0,1,2}² together with a matching upper bound (le_antisymm of the construction and an exhaustive impossibility argument).

sections.title: Part VIII-B: f₃(3) = 9 — Hybrid Computation
sections.summary: f3_3 : f3 3 = 9 via le_antisymm f3_3_le_9 f3_3_ge_9 — a hybrid of explicit construction (lower bound) and a combinatorial counting argument (upper bound).

sections.title: Part VIII-B2: f₃(4) = 20 — Explicit Construction + Meshulam
sections.summary: f3_4 : f3 4 = 20 via le_antisymm f3_4_le_20 f3_4_ge_20, combining an explicit 20-point cap set with a Meshulam-style upper bound.

sections.title: Part VIII-C: Generalized Binary Cube (f₃(n) ≥ 2ⁿ)
sections.summary: boolToZMod3, boolEmbed and boolEmbed_injective embed the Boolean cube {0,1}ⁿ into {0,1,2}ⁿ; binaryCubeImg has card 2ⁿ (binaryCubeImg_card) and is a cap set (binaryCubeImg_isCapSet), yielding f3_ge_two_pow : f3 n ≥ 2ⁿ.

sections.title: Part VIII-D: Product Structure (Supermultiplicativity)
sections.summary: vecConcat and finsetProduct build product cap sets; isCapSet_product shows the product of cap sets is a cap set with finsetProduct_card = |A|·|B|, giving f3_supermultiplicative : f3 (m+n) ≥ f3 m · f3 n. Corollaries f3_monotone and f3_doubling (f3 (n+1) ≥ 2·f3 n).

sections.title: Part VIII-E: Derived Bounds from Product Structure
sections.summary: Concrete lower bounds derived from supermultiplicativity and the small-case values: f3_5_ge_40, f3_6_ge_81, f3_6_ge_80, f3_7_ge_180, f3_8_ge_400.

sections.title: Part VIII-F: General Power Lower Bound
sections.summary: f3_power_lower_bound : f3 (k·n) ≥ f3 n ^ k, the general power form of supermultiplicativity, and f3_exponential_gap quantifying the exponential separation between the 2ⁿ lower bound and the 3ⁿ ambient size.

sections.title: Part IX: Summary
sections.summary: Headline theorems: erdos_185 ((fun n => f3 n) =o[atTop] (fun n => 3ⁿ)), erdos_185_density (density → 0), and erdos_185_answer packaging the resolution of Erdős problem #185.

crossReferences.description: Erdős #140 concerns 3-AP-free sets in {1,...,N} (Kelley-Meka 2023); cap sets in {0,1,2}^n are the finite geometry analogue, with the connection f₃(n) ≥ R₃(N) formalized here
Both concern extremal density problems: #180 for forbidden graph substructures, #185 for forbidden collinear triples in finite geometry

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #185 asked whether f₃(n) = o(3^n), where f₃(n) is the maximum cap set in {0,1,2}^n. The answer is YES, proved as a corollary of the density Hales-Jewett theorem (Furstenberg-Katznelson 1991). More recent work by Ellenberg-Gijswijt (2016) showed f₃(n) ≤ c^n with c < 3, a major quantitative improvement.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: **Additive Combinatorics Connections:**

1. **Cap Set Problem:** Central problem in finite geometry and coding theory.

2. **Hales-Jewett Theorem:** Fundamental result in Ramsey theory.

**3. Polynomial Method:** Ellenberg-Gijswijt's proof revolutionized the field.

4. **Sunflower Conjecture:** Cap set bounds have implications for other problems.

5. **Coding Theory:** Cap sets relate to error-correcting codes over F₃.
openQuestions: What is $\lim_{n\to\infty} f_3(n)^{1/n}$? Known: between $\approx 2.217$ (Edel lower bound) and $\approx 2.756$ (Ellenberg-Gijswijt)
Can the Croot-Lev-Pach polynomial method be improved to match the lower bound?
Analogous cap set problems over $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ for $q > 3$: what is $\lim f_q(n)^{1/n}$?
Is there an explicit construction of cap sets of size $c^n$ for any $c > 2.217$?
Does the density Hales-Jewett theorem have a purely combinatorial proof (avoiding ergodic theory)?
